preamble: The velar nasal [ŋ] is replaced by the glottal fricative [h] in the Huastecan branch of Mayan: Proto-Mayan *ŋ appears as h in Huastec and Chicomuceltec, at least word-finally, so that Proto-Mayan *q'iiŋ 'sun, day' corresponds to Huastec k'ih. The change removes both nasality and oral place of articulation.

examples.note: Huastecan reflects Proto-Mayan *ŋ as h word-finally; Chicomuceltec also has k'ih, and Huastec tak'in 'silver, money' with -n is therefore explained as a loan from a lowland Mayan language.

sources: Mora-Marín, D. (2024). Brief Comments on taʔ=k'in 'metal' and Its Culture Historical Implications. University of North Carolina. https://davidmm.web.unc.edu/2024/03/11/note-35/
Norcliffe, E. (2003). The Reconstruction of Proto-Huastecan. MA thesis, University of Canterbury. https://glottolog.org/resource/reference/id/109784
